title: older than ... more expensive than ...
summary: Слово **than** после сравнительной степени («старше, чем …»), а также **a bit / much / a lot** для усиления и смягчения сравнения.
ru:
## than = «чем»
Когда мы называем второго участника сравнения, после сравнительной степени ставим **than**.
> Athens is **older than** Rome. — Афины старше, чем Рим.
> Are oranges **more expensive than** bananas? — Апельсины дороже бананов?
> It's **easier to phone than to write**. — Проще позвонить, чем писать.

## than + местоимение
После **than** в разговоре обычно ставим форму **me / him / her / us / them**. Но можно сказать и полным предложением.
> I can run **faster than him**. = I can run faster than **he can**.
> You are a better singer **than me**. = ... than **I am**.
> She got up earlier **than us**. = ... than **we did**.

## more than / less than
Можно сравнивать и количество.
> It cost **more than** £30. — Это стоило больше 30 фунтов.
> The film was **less than** an hour. — Фильм шёл меньше часа.
> You go out **more than me**. — Ты выходишь гулять чаще, чем я.

## a bit / much / a lot / far
Чтобы показать, **насколько** разница, ставим слово перед сравнительной степенью.
- **a bit**, **a little**, **slightly** — чуть-чуть
- **much**, **a lot**, **far** — намного
> Box A is **a bit bigger** than Box B. — Коробка А чуть больше.
> Canada is **much bigger** than France. — Канада намного больше Франции.
> The hotel was **much more expensive** than I expected. — Отель был гораздо дороже, чем я ожидала.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~older as Rome~~ → older **than** Rome
- ~~more big than~~ → **bigger than**
- ~~very bigger~~ → **much bigger** (very с сравнительной степенью не ставим)
- ~~more good than~~ → **better than**
en:
## than
When we name the second thing in a comparison, we use **than** after the comparative.
> Athens is **older than** Rome.
> Are oranges **more expensive than** bananas?
> It's **easier to phone than to write**.

## than + pronoun
After **than** we usually say **me / him / her / us / them** in speaking. You can also use a full clause.
> I can run **faster than him**. = I can run faster than **he can**.
> You are a better singer **than me**. = ... than **I am**.

## more than / less than
We can compare amounts too.
> It cost **more than** £30.
> The film was **less than** an hour.
> You go out **more than me**.

## a bit / much / a lot
We put these words before the comparative to show the size of the difference.
- **a bit**, **a little**, **slightly** — a small difference
- **much**, **a lot**, **far** — a big difference
> Box A is **a bit bigger** than Box B.
> Canada is **much bigger** than France.

## Common mistakes
- ~~older as Rome~~ → older **than** Rome
- ~~very bigger~~ → **much bigger**
- ~~more good than~~ → **better than**
structure:
## Формула
> Подлежащее + be + **comparative** + **than** + то, с чем сравниваем
> My sister is **taller than** me. · This bag is **more expensive than** that one.

## Усиление и смягчение
| Слово | Смысл | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| a bit / a little / slightly | чуть-чуть | a bit older than me |
| much / a lot / far | намного | much more difficult than I thought |

## После than
| Разговорная форма | Полная форма |
|---|---|
| than **me** | than **I am / do** |
| than **him / her** | than **he / she is / does** |
| than **us / them** | than **we / they are / do** |

## Количество
- **more than** 50 people — больше 50 человек
- **less than** an hour — меньше часа
- **more** money **than** I need — больше денег, чем мне нужно

exercises.title: Сравните людей
exercises.instruction: Вставьте сравнительную степень слова в скобках и **than**.
exercises.example: Tom is 25. Ann is 22. Tom is **older than** Ann.

items.text: Kate is 1.70 m tall. Ben is 1.80 m. Ben is {{taller than}} Kate.
Sara gets up at 6. Max gets up at 8. Sara gets up {{earlier than}} Max.
I pay 300 euros. My friend pays 400 euros. My friend's flat is {{more expensive than}} mine.
Anna is a very good dancer. I'm not. Anna is a {{better}} dancer {{than}} me.
A bus takes 20 minutes. A taxi takes 10 minutes. A taxi is {{faster than}} a bus.
A cat is 4 kg. A dog is 20 kg. A dog is {{heavier than}} a cat.

exercises.title: much или a bit?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте **a bit** (небольшая разница) или **much** (большая разница) и сравнительную степень.

items.text: My sister is 20 and I am 21. I'm {{a bit older}} than her.
A car costs £15,000. A bike costs £300. A car is {{much more expensive}} than a bike.
Today it's 21 degrees. Yesterday it was 20. Today is {{a bit warmer}}.
Moscow has 12 million people. Bishkek has 1 million. Moscow is {{much bigger}} than Bishkek.
My room is 15 metres. Yours is 14. Mine is {{a bit bigger}}.

items.why: Перед сравнительной степенью: **a lot / much**, но не very.

items.q: The test was ___ than I expected.

items.why: В разговоре: than **me** (или than I do).

options: He runs more fast than me.

items.q: Как сказать «Он чуть старше, чем она»?
options: He's a bit older than her.
He's a bit more old than her.
He's a bit older that her.
